diagram:BV.description: Metric BV perimeter and half-mass Cheeger interfaces on the actual closed intrinsic support are defined. Complement symmetry is formalized for finite Borel measures on metric spaces, including the closed intrinsic support law; the zero-dimensional convention and an infinite-measure counterexample are proved. The half-mass and symmetric BV Cheeger constants are proved equal on every probability metric space. For a finite measure, globally Lipschitz approximants converging in global L1 may replace bounded-support tests and bound the perimeter, and on a proper metric space so may locally Lipschitz approximants (even under L1 convergence on every closed ball only, through clamping), the relaxation infima over both classes being equal to the perimeter (finite measures; the locally Lipschitz class on proper spaces with global or compact-set L1 convergence, in particular on the closed intrinsic support of every finite-dimensional law); epsilon recovery tests exist below every threshold above the perimeter, and every finite perimeter is the limit of the costs of an explicitly selected approximating sequence (for any Borel measure; nothing is claimed for infinite perimeter); the perimeter is sequentially lower semicontinuous under global L1 convergence of measurable set indicators for every Borel measure; for every probability law on a metric space it is at most the outer Minkowski content of every measurable set (one inequality, via two-radius plateau ramps), and the Minkowski coarea inequality holds with the actual local slope for every globally Lipschitz function, bounding the integrated superlevel content and BV perimeter of every test by its cost; every test has a quantitative superlevel selection with content at most cost/(1-2 delta) + epsilon and indicator error at most its L1 error over delta. For every set of finite BV perimeter, explicit measurable superlevel sets converge to it in L1 with Minkowski contents converging to its perimeter (Minkowski recovery), and the relaxed lower Minkowski content, the infimum of liminf outer contents over measurable sets converging in L1, equals the perimeter for every set; for measurable sets of mass strictly between 0 and 1 the recovery masses converge, eventually stay in (0, 1), and the symmetric Cheeger quotients converge to the BV quotient. The symmetric and half-mass BV Cheeger constants equal the Minkowski Cheeger constant for every probability law on a normed space, and for the intrinsic coordinate law they equal the isoperimetric constant (an equality of infima; the pointwise reverse inequality is false in general). Restriction to the closed measure support does not increase the metric BV perimeter of the trace of a set (one inequality, via restricted tests and the isometric-inclusion slope bound), with equality under an actual nonexpansive retraction onto a full-mass measurable subset, in particular, via the nearest-point projection, for every probability law on a Hilbert space with convex closed support, where the half-mass and symmetric BV Cheeger constants of the law and of its closed-support law agree. For every finite-dimensional log-concave probability law, the BV Cheeger constant on the closed intrinsic support therefore equals the isoperimetric constant. The upper Minkowski content, the limsup of the same radius quotient, is at least the lower content; for every set the real mass of its open s-thickening is monotone, hence differentiable at Lebesgue-almost every radius, at every differentiability radius the upper content of that thickening is at most the derivative, and the upper content of the s-thickening integrated over s in (0, r) is at most the mass increment nu(B^r) - nu(B) for every set and every radius (probability laws on normed groups; inequalities only, with no measurability of the content, integrability of the derivative or absolute continuity of the radius mass assumed). Every measurable set of finite lower content is recovered by thickenings converging in L1 with limsup of upper contents at most its lower content; every set of finite BV perimeter is recovered by measurable sets converging in L1 whose upper contents tend to its perimeter; and the relaxed upper Minkowski content, the infimum of liminf upper contents over the same measurable approximating class, equals the perimeter for every set, hence the relaxed lower content (equalities of infima; the pointwise upper content is not identified with the perimeter). This content chain (both contents, the local-slope Minkowski coarea inequality, the bridge, both recoveries and both relaxed identities) holds on arbitrary metric spaces with a Borel probability law, the generic coarea using the lower semicontinuous open-ball supremum; since the evening of 2026-09-30 the chain holds for every finite Borel measure (scaling by nonnegative real scalars, the zero measure, normalization of a finite nonzero measure, both recoveries and both relaxed identities at finite total mass, arbitrary targets). This ✓ covers exactly that log-concave (convex-support) identification for the bounded-support relaxation; The locally Lipschitz classes on nonproper spaces, nonconvex support transfer, general metric-measure/RCD comparisons and dimension-free KLS remain open. A supporting test-cost estimate uses closed function support mass rather than total mass: every bounded-support test has finite cost under a measure finite on bounded Borel sets, including infinite total mass. The actual globally Lipschitz relaxation with global L1 convergence equals the bounded-support perimeter for every measurable finite-mass target under any Borel measure on a metric space, using cutoff bounds by the original indicator error and target-tail mass; this bounded-support reduction neither requires properness nor identifies a Minkowski relaxation. The direct positive-superlevel local-slope coarea bound holds when a positive-support neighborhood has finite measure, and its all-level version holds for nonnegative functions; restriction to that neighborhood preserves lower content at positive superlevels. For any Borel measure the perimeter/content bridge holds at measurable finite-mass targets. The full Lemma 3.2 chain is formalized with the actual right-radius liminf of integrated open-ball growth between positive-level content and original local-slope integrals, under nonnegativity and finite positive-support-neighborhood mass. Actual bounded measurable lower-recovery sets have finite mass and finite lower content term by term, converge in global indicator L1 and have contents converging to perimeter at measurable finite-mass targets under measures finite on bounded Borel sets. The existing relaxed lower-content infimum equals perimeter at that scope, including infinite perimeter; finite prefixes with infinite mass remain allowed because convergence ensures eventual finite mass. Finite target mass and finite lower content imply a finite-mass positive neighborhood. Radius-local restriction and a tail of small radii prove actual lower-to-upper recovery with original global indicator L1 convergence. Diagonal selection gives bounded open finite-mass upper-recovery sets with finite upper content and contents converging to finite perimeter. The existing relaxed upper infimum equals perimeter, hence the lower relaxation, at the published finite-mass Borel target scope, including infinite perimeter by order and infinite-mass finite prefixes. Lemma 2.1 also exposes relaxed upper content <= lower content at measurable finite-mass targets under any Borel measure. Nonconvex support transfer, locally Lipschitz classes on nonproper spaces and general RCD comparisons remain separate; no ledger promotion is claimed. Lemma 2.1's equality of the relaxed lower and upper Minkowski contents also holds for every Borel measure at measurable finite-mass targets (2026-10-01), and on proper metric spaces the Remark 3.5 locally Lipschitz relaxations with global or compact-set L1 convergence equal the bounded-support perimeter at measurable finite-mass targets for every Borel measure (2026-10-01).

lem:bkl-near-symmetric-gradient.description: Bizeul–Klartag–Lehec Lemma 3.2: ∇₀h_{i+1} is within χ_i/λ (squared L² distance) of a field symmetric in its first two indices, for a pair satisfying (30) with α² ≥ λ > 0.

lem:bkl-generator-temperate.description: Bizeul–Klartag–Lehec Lemma 2.1 step: the L² class of a function of temperate growth lies in the generator domain with A[f] = [−ℒf]; a centered temperate solution of −ℒu = g is the centered inverse of [g].

lem:bkl-poincare-temperate.description: Bizeul–Klartag–Lehec (20), (32), Lemma 3.2 in the heat model: Poincaré on the class 𝒜, ‖∇h‖² ≤ C‖ℒh‖², α² ≥ 1/C for a pair, and Lemma 3.2 with λ = 1/C.

lem:bkl-suspension-convexity.description: The finite-copy suspension potential (109) is continuous and convex under the Hessian condition (110); a positive finite copy number exists (a supporting step of BKL Proposition 7.1).

lem:bkl-laplace-law.description: The Laplace noise η_β of BKL Proposition 7.1: law, local moment generating function β²/(β²−w²) on |w|<β, mean 0, second moment 2/β², polynomial moments, and the vanishing derivative of its log-MGF at 0.

lem:bkl-suspension-law.description: The joint law of (S, X₁, …, X_N) in BKL Proposition 7.1: a probability measure with density proportional to e^{−W_N} (109), log-concave under (110), with an exponential moment and a smooth logarithmic Laplace transform near 0.

lem:bkl-suspension-isotropy.description: Isotropy of the joint law of the suspension from the normalization (108) of f (BKL Proposition 7.1, p. 28).

lem:bkl-suspension-derivatives.description: BKL (111)–(112) for the chosen N: factorization of Λ_ν, its first derivative along e₀ at points with vanishing S-coordinate, and the mixed cumulant entries d!/(σ√N)·T_d f(e_J) on single copy blocks.

lem:bkl-coordinate-adapter.description: Transport of isotropy and cumulants along linear isometries, the cumulant hypothesis on the joint space, the Hilbert–Schmidt step after (112) and the β → ∞ limit (BKL Proposition 7.1, pp. 29–30).

lem:bkl-affine-orthogonal.description: Affine-orthogonal decomposition in L²(μ) for a centered law with identity covariance: centering, orthogonality, L², C² with the same Hessian, contraction and Bessel; the linear-function step in any orthonormal basis (BKL Proposition 7.1, p. 30).

lem:bkl-cumulant-envelope.description: Section 6 envelope arithmetic of BKL: b_m = K^{m−1}((m−1)!)², identities (105)–(106), the absorption after (106) and the contraction (101)–(102); the cumulant induction itself is the cutoff energy induction (lem:bkl-cutoff-energy).

lem:bkl-quadratic-tilt.description: Normalized small quadratic tilts of a probability measure converge to it (integrals, weak convergence, first and second moments): the second step of BKL's regular approximation (Section 2).

lem:bkl-suspension-taylor-bound.description: BKL (113): under the cumulant hypothesis in every dimension, |T_d f|² ≤ b/(d!)²·‖f‖₂² for every f ∈ L²(μ) orthogonal to the affine functions (smooth normalized case via the suspension and β → ∞, then density).

lem:letwin-support-identities.description: Letwin's Lemma A.3 (weighted directional integration by parts under e^{−φ}dm, any direction) and the finite form of equation (2.12) for symmetric arrays with arbitrary real weights; supports of BKL Lemma 4.2 through the Letwin bound, not Theorem 2.5.

lem:letwin-mapped-covariance.description: Letwin, proof of Theorem 1.2, p. 14, the covariance step preceding (2.21), reviewed stronger: for an isotropic law of X on ℝⁿ and every real symmetric M (singular, indefinite, n = 0), Z = |M|^{1/2} X has Cov(Z) = |M|; with the functional-calculus root, sign factorization |M|^{1/2} sgn(M) |M|^{1/2} = M and sgn(M)² = Id for invertible M. Not the Stein-kernel identity (2.21), Theorem 2.5 or Theorem 1.2.

lem:letwin-cutoff-profile.description: Letwin Lemma A.4 (p. 17), real-variable part: the cutoff profile η(t) = smoothTransition(2 − t) (smooth, antitone, [0,1]-valued, 1 for t ≤ 1, 0 for t ≥ 2; η′ and η″ vanish off [1,2], are compactly supported and share a bound B), a smooth compactly supported nonnegative majorant w ≥ |η″| vanishing for t ≤ 0 and t ≥ 3, and the monotone exhaustion η(a/(n+1)) ↑ 1 for every real a, also along real R (R ↦ η(a/R) monotone on (0, ∞), limit 1); the tail primitive q_R(t) = R⁻¹∫_{t/R}^3 w of a smooth nonnegative w vanishing off (0,3), for R > 0 (smooth, q_R′ = −R⁻² w(t/R), 0 ≤ q_R ≤ R⁻¹∫_0^3 w, q_R = 0 for t ≥ 3R); the affine rescaling (f((·−c)/R))′ = R⁻¹ f′((·−c)/R), ″ = R⁻² f″((·−c)/R) for arbitrary f, c, R (total-derivative conventions). Immediate consumer: the Lemma A.4 cutoffs η((φ − min φ + 1)/R) with O(1/R) generator defect → Lemma A.5 → Theorem 2.5 → Theorem 1.2 → BKL Lemma 4.2; Lemma A.4 (lem:letwin-a4-cutoffs) and Lemma A.5 for given cutoffs (lem:letwin-a5-cutoffs) are provided, Theorems 2.5 and 1.2 are not.

lem:letwin-inverse-hessian-quadratic.description: Letwin Lemma A.4 (p. 17) support: for a C² potential φ with positive definite Hessian at x, every orthonormal basis (any rank) and all coefficients a, Σ_ij ((∇²φ(x))⁻¹)_ij a_i a_j ≥ 0 — the sign of the φ^{ij}∂_iW∂_jW term in Lχ_R. Immediate consumer: the pointwise generator-defect domination of the A.4 cutoffs; Lemma A.4 and A.5 for given cutoffs are lem:letwin-a4-cutoffs and lem:letwin-a5-cutoffs; the moment map and Theorems 2.5/1.2 are not provided.

prop:bkl-suspension.description: BKL Proposition 7.1, (107), in the source form: if R^ν_{d+1} ≤ b·Id for every isotropic log-concave ν in every dimension (d ≥ 2, b > 0), then every isotropic regular law satisfies |T_d f|² ≤ 2b/(d!)²·‖f‖₂² for all f ∈ L²(μ). Conditional on its own hypothesis, which the certified Theorem 4.1 (thm:bkl-cumulant-bound) supplies in BKL Theorem 1.1.

lem:bkl-weak-limit-transfer.description: Weak-limit transfer of the Poincaré bound (BKL Section 2, p. 5): the smooth-test bound passes to weak limits on compactly supported smooth tests, extends to all admissible tests by cutoffs, and bounds the literature constant of a log-concave limit law by the limit constant.

lem:bkl-gaussian-hessian-upper.description: Upper Hessian bound of the Gaussian-smoothed potential (BKL Section 2, p. 5): ∇²V_s(x)(v,v) = 2s‖v‖² − 4s² Var_{P_x}⟪·,v⟫ ≤ 2s‖v‖² through the Gaussian posterior, with the posterior variance bound ‖v‖²/(2s) and finite second moments.

lem:bkl-borell-uniform-moments.description: Quantitative Borell moment bounds: a ball of mass ≥ 3/4 and radius R gives ∫e^{q‖v‖} ≤ 3^{3/4}/(1−3^{−1/4}) with q = log 3/(4R) and all-order moment bounds; the radius 2√(M+1) is constructed from a second-moment bound ∫‖v‖² ≤ M; isotropic log-concave laws on ℝⁿ as a consumer.

lem:bkl-gaussian-posterior-moments.description: Gaussian posterior of the smoothing (BKL Section 2, p. 5): log-concave with explicit Borell density; centered version with mean zero, directional variance ≤ ‖v‖²/(2s), trace ≤ n/(2s), and exponential/all-order moment bounds uniform in the base point.

lem:bkl-gaussian-growth.description: Polynomial growth of all derivatives of the Gaussian-smoothed potential (BKL Section 2, p. 5): centered-posterior factorization, Dⁿ V = −(2s)ⁿ Dⁿ Λ_{Q_x}(0) for n ≥ 3, uniform Borell moments, local log composition and the temperate-growth constructor.

lem:bkl-regular-producer.description: The regular approximation produces a regular potential (BKL (12)): V_s + δ/2‖·‖² has δ·Id ≤ ∇² ≤ (2s+δ)·Id and polynomial growth; its law is the two-step law (Gaussian smoothing then quadratic tilt) and is log-concave.

lem:letwin-stein-dual.description: Letwin Stein kernels (Definition 2.6), the H^{-1} dual norm (2.19), the locally Lipschitz extension A.7 and Lemma 2.9 for full-dimensional log-concave laws.

lem:bkl-regular-affine.description: Regular potentials under affine changes of variables (BKL Section 2): V∘(L·+c) is regular with constants a/(1+‖L⁻¹‖)² and max(b,1)(1+‖L‖)²; its law is the image of the law of V under y ↦ L⁻¹(y−c) and the normalizer scales by |det L|⁻¹.

lem:bkl-regular-reduction.description: BKL p. 30 conditional reduction: under CumulantBound d ((d!)² K^d) for all d ≥ 2 (Theorem 4.1), every isotropic regular law has C_P ≤ 2·C_{3.1}·K, via Theorem 3.1 with R = √(2K), Proposition 7.1 for d ≥ 2 and the Bessel bound for d = 1. The hypothesis is discharged in BKL Theorem 1.1 (thm:bkl-poincare).

lem:bkl-gaussian-moments.description: Moments and weak convergence of the Gaussian smoothing (BKL Section 2): γ_s has mean 0 and ∫⟪v,y⟫² = ‖v‖²/(2s); Cov(μ*γ_s) = Cov μ + Id/(2s); means, second moments and covariances converge as s → ∞; μ*γ_{n+1} → μ weakly.

lem:bkl-regular-isotropic.description: Regular laws reduce to isotropic regular laws (BKL Section 2): finite second moment, full support, positive definite covariance, and an affine centering/whitening preserving regularity with explicit image law.

lem:letwin-mean-hessian.description: Letwin Lemma 2.3, analytic part for a given smooth convex potential φ with e^{-φ} a probability density: Hessian entries integrable (cutoff IBP, uniform bound, Fatou, polarization), ∫∂_u∂_vφ dν = ∫∂_uφ∂_vφ dν, and = ⟪u,v⟫ when (∇φ)_*ν is isotropic.

lem:bkl-quadratic-covariance.description: Covariance of the quadratic tilt μ.tilted(−δ‖·‖²/2) converges to Cov μ in operator norm as δ → 0⁺ for laws with finite second moment (BKL Section 2).

lem:bkl-regular-isometry.description: Regular potentials under linear isometries between finite-dimensional inner product spaces: same constants, image law, isotropy and Poincaré constants preserved; standard coordinates on ℝⁿ and transfer of a Euclidean regular-isotropic bound (BKL Section 2).

lem:bkl-regular-approximation.description: Joint Gaussian-then-quadratic regular approximation (BKL Section 2): laws of regular potentials V_{n+1} + δ_k/2‖·‖² converge weakly to μ along a selected diagonal, with means, raw second moments and covariance operators converging; generic metric diagonal selection.

lem:bkl-regular-poincare-transfer.description: Conditional Poincaré transfer (BKL Section 2): a universal bound K on isotropic regular laws gives C_P ≤ K‖Cov‖ for every regular law, by centering/whitening and covariance-energy transport; envelope coefficient K(1+‖Cov−Id‖) → K.

lem:bkl-isotropic-reduction.description: Reduction of the isotropic log-concave Poincaré bound to isotropic regular laws (BKL Section 2, complete): Borell density and full support from isotropy, regular approximants with converging covariances, envelope transfer, weak-limit passage; KLS.IsotropicBound K from a bound for isotropic regular laws on ℝⁿ. With the p. 30 reduction: Theorem 1.1 conditional on Theorem 4.1 (no certificate).

lem:letwin-hessian-kernel.description: Letwin Lemma 2.7, analytic part for a given potential: τ = ∇²φ ∘ (∇φ)⁻¹ is a symmetric, positive semidefinite, integrable Stein kernel of the isotropic gradient image law with mean Id, given gradient injectivity; moment-map existence, strict PD and HS-L² not provided.

lem:letwin-diffusion-product-rule.description: Letwin (2.3): the nondivergence operator L_{A,b} f = Σ A_ij ∂_ij f − Σ b_i ∂_i f for an arbitrary symmetric coefficient field, its Leibniz rule L(fg) = f Lg + g Lf + 2 Σ A_ij ∂_i f ∂_j g, and the generic Hessian product rule; the inverse-Hessian specialization and Theorem 2.5 are not provided.

lem:letwin-inverse-hessian-derivative.description: Letwin (2.5) and the inverse-Hessian (2.3) operator for a given smooth φ with positive definite Hessian: Hessian operator a self-adjoint unit with positive inverse, derivative of the inverse Hessian (operator and coordinate forms), Leibniz rule of L = Σ (∇²φ)⁻¹_ij ∂_ij − Σ (∂_iV∘∇φ) ∂_i, and the right-hand-side derivative of the Monge–Ampère log-det equation taken as a hypothesis. Jacobi, Lemma 2.4/2.6, PSD, Brascamp–Lieb and moment-map existence not provided.

lem:letwin-monge-ampere-first.description: Jacobi's formula for det/log det and Letwin (2.4): for a given smooth φ with positive definite Hessian and the zero-order Monge–Ampère equation log det ∇²φ = −φ + V∘∇φ (hypothesis), Σ (∇²φ)⁻¹_ac ∂_iac φ = −∂_iφ + Σ ∂_aV(∇φ) ∂_ai φ, with V smooth near the closure of K ⊇ range ∇φ. Moment-map existence not provided.

lem:letwin-monge-ampere-second.description: Letwin (2.6): L(∂_ij φ) + ∂_ij φ = (∇²φ ∇²V(∇φ) ∇²φ)_ij + inverse-Hessian-weighted third-derivative Gram, under the zero-order equation; both right-hand matrices positive semidefinite (V convex on the open K; Gram via A⊗A). Derivative commutation from C² symmetry. No Theorem 2.5/BL/P2.8/HS-norm/root claim.

lem:bkl-posterior-parameter-response.description: BKL p. 19, (67): deterministic parameter response of the posterior μ e^{⟨c,x⟩ − ½⟨Qx,x⟩}/Z — compact prior (all (c,Q) including 0; uniform moments) and coercive Q with any prior and polynomial statistics; covariance derivative along parameter lines; isotropic initial response ⟨u,h⟩. No SDE, Itô or martingale statement.

lem:bkl-coefficients-regularity.description: BKL (67), compact stage: joint C^∞ in (c,Q) of the posterior expectation, mean and covariance of a compactly supported prior (all finite pairs incl. Q = 0, non-symmetric Q, rank 0); for an isotropic prior the rate Cov⁻¹ and the drift Cov⁻¹a are jointly C^∞ and the diffusion coefficient Cov⁻¹ᐟ² and the triple (Cov⁻¹ᐟ², Cov⁻¹a, Cov⁻¹) are locally Lipschitz on the whole parameter space (Sylvester Frobenius estimate for positive roots, relative CFC continuity, local floors). No strong solution, non-explosion, Itô or Theorem 4.1 claim.

lem:letwin-inverse-hessian-ibp.description: Letwin (2.2) for a GIVEN smooth φ with PD Hessian, ∫e^{−φ} = 1 and the zero-order MA equation (V smooth on an open set ⊇ range ∇φ): divergence of the inverse Hessian, flux form Σ_i ∂_i(e^{−φ}A_ij) = −e^{−φ}∂_jV(∇φ), density divergence form of L, and the weighted IBP ∫(Lf)g dν = −∫Σ A_ij ∂_if ∂_jg dν for smooth f,g with one compactly supported; ∫Lf dν = 0; integrated symmetry on compact tests. The noncompact extension is lem:letwin-a4-cutoffs and lem:letwin-a5-cutoffs. No moment-map producer, closed L² generator, Brascamp–Lieb, Theorem 2.5 or Proposition 2.8.

lem:bkl-cgf-gradient-jets.description: BKL p. 20 before (74): for the CGF Λ of a compactly supported law, ∇Λ(0) = ∫x dμ, D(∇Λ − ∇Λ(0))(0) = Cov μ and, for every r ≥ 1, Dʳ(∇Λ − ∇Λ(0))(0)[h] = cumulantVector μ h (⟪·,w⟫ = κ_{r+1}(h,w), w in the last slot); generic supports Dʳ(f − c) = Dʳf and ⟪Dʳ∇f[h],w⟫ = Dʳ⁺¹f[h,w]; principal root sandwich σAσ = Id. (74) drift and stochastic statements not provided. Cumulant tensors of a compactly supported law are symmetric under every slot permutation.

lem:bkl-localization-supports.description: BKL (67)–(68) deterministic supports: covariance Cauchy–Schwarz cov(X,Y)² ≤ Var X·Var Y on any probability space; Var⟪Sh,·⟫ = ‖h‖² for a self-adjoint S with the actual sandwich S·Cov·S = Id (hypothesis, no root produced); trace energy Σ_i (tr B_i)² ≤ n Σ_{ijk} (B_i)_{jk}² without symmetry; third-moment contraction Σ_{ijk} (∫x_i x_j x_k)² ≤ ∫‖x‖⁶ (integrable sixth moment, no centering); covariance radius ‖Cov μ_{c,Q}‖ ≤ r² for a prior supported in the closed r-ball (all finite (c,Q), no isotropy). No noise bound, covariance dynamics, Itô, strong solution or non-explosion claim. The third-moment contraction also holds for an a.e.-measurable random vector on any probability space.

lem:bkl-canonical-standardisation.description: BKL (67)–(68), transported law of (75)–(77): for a compact isotropic prior and every finite (c,Q) incl. rank 0 and negative Q, the principal inverse square root Cov(μ_{c,Q})^{-1/2} is a continuous linear equivalence W = σ and the image of the centred posterior under W is isotropic (L², mean 0, Cov = Id). Same principal root, no driver rotation, SDE, Itô, non-explosion or Theorem 4.1 claim.

lem:bkl-noise-bound.description: BKL (68): for a compact isotropic prior, a measurable statistic with |f| ≤ C on the prior support and every finite (c,Q) incl. signed non-symmetric Q and rank 0, ‖D_c(∫f dμ_{·,Q})(c) ∘ Cov(μ_{c,Q})^{-1/2}‖² ≤ Var_{μ_{c,Q}} f ≤ C² with the same principal root as (67). Deterministic coefficient bound only; no stochastic integral, Itô, martingale or quadratic variation.

lem:iterated-derivative-symmetry-leibniz.description: Generic supports for the BKL cumulant algebra (71)–(74): raw iterated derivatives of a globally C^∞ map between real normed spaces are symmetric under every slot permutation (directional list convention = iteratedFDeriv, real C² symmetry), and D^m(B(f,g))[h] = Σ over Boolean subset indicators of B(D^{|q|}f[h_q], D^{m−|q|}g[h_{¬q}]) with coefficient 1 and inherited slot order (no factorial). Ordered-mask partition: the two selections have lengths adding to m and together permute the slots, a one-slot indicator selects exactly that slot, and a length-one selection comes from such an indicator (repeated values and m = 0 included). The (74) expansion and grouping are separate nodes; no parameter jet or stochastic claim. Complement pairing of Boolean masks (twice the sum over masks selecting a fixed slot).

lem:moment-tails-eighth.description: Ball-conditioning supports (Letwin A.1 approximation dependency): for a probability law on a normed group with integrable ‖x‖⁸ and R > 0, ν(B(0,R)ᶜ) ≤ M₈/R⁸ (Markov), ‖x‖⁴ plus its tail restriction are integrable with ∫_{B(0,R)ᶜ} ‖x‖⁴ ≤ M₈/R⁴, and 2M₈ ≤ R⁸ gives ν(B(0,R)) ≥ 1/2 > 0 (M₈ the actual eighth moment; open ball; R > 0 indispensable). No covariance convergence or whitening claim.

lem:ball-conditioning.description: Letwin A.1 conditioning step: conditionOnBall ν R hp = Mathlib cond on the open ball B(0,R) of positive mass p (a definition domain, not a conclusion premise); for integrable ‖x‖⁸, R > 0, C ≥ 0 and measurable f with |f| ≤ C(1+‖x‖⁴): f integrable under ν and ν_B, |E_B f − E f| ≤ ((1−p)|E f| + ∫_{Bᶜ}|f|)/p ≤ (C/p)((1−p)(2+∫‖x‖⁴) + M₈/R⁴). No smoothing, covariance convergence or whitening claim.

lem:bkl-posterior-sixth-moment.description: Canonical sixth moment: for a compact isotropic log-concave prior on ℝⁿ, every c and every self-adjoint PSD Q, Y = Cov(μ_{c,Q})^{-1/2}(x − a) has integrable |Y|⁶ and ∫|Y|⁶ dμ_{c,Q} ≤ 6!(log 3/(8√(n+1)))^{-6}·3^{3/4}/(1−3^{-1/4}) (explicit, dimension-dependent). Signed or non-self-adjoint Q is outside the statement. No (69) identity, INTERFACE C energies or stochastic claim.

lem:bkl-singleton-allocation.description: BKL p. 21 singleton terms of (74): for a compactly supported law with invertible covariance A, ⟨κ₂(w,·), A⁻¹κ_{k+1}(h₁..h_k,·)⟩ = κ_{k+1}(h₁..h_k, w) (order k+1, w in the last slot). The full (74) expansion and its grouping are separate nodes; no parameter jet or stochastic claim.

lem:bkl-raw-drift-expansion.description: BKL p. 21 (74) at a fixed compactly supported law: for ANY continuous linear M, D^m⟨v,Mv⟩(0)[h] = Σ over nonempty proper subsets J of ⟨κ_{|J|+1}(h_J,·), M κ_{m−|J|+1}(h_{Jᶜ},·)⟩ (coefficient 1, no factorial; empty/full vanish by v(0) = 0), with the jets of v at 0, the Leibniz rule for ⟨f, Mg⟩ and the empty-mask criterion. The grouping for M = A⁻¹ is lem:bkl-grouped-drift-expansion; no parameter jet or stochastic claim.

lem:bkl-grouped-drift-expansion.description: BKL pp. 20–21, deterministic spatial step of the proof of Lemma 4.3: for a compactly supported law with invertible covariance A, every m ≥ 3, all h (repeated directions allowed) and any slot i₀, D^m⟨v, A⁻¹v⟩(0)[h] = 2m κ_m(h) + 2 Σ over J ∋ i₀ with |J|, |Jᶜ| ≥ 2 of ⟨κ_{|J|+1}(h_J,·), A⁻¹κ_{m−|J|+1}(h_{Jᶜ},·)⟩, i.e. (74) grouped as 2m κ_m + 2 L_m with L_m from (72) (any representative slot). No stochastic differential (73), Eldan process or Itô claim.

lem:bkl-noise-entries.description: BKL p. 19 (69) deterministic entry identity: for a compact isotropic prior and every finite (c,Q) incl. signed non-symmetric Q, (P H_i P)_{jk} = ∫ (σV)_j(σV)_k(σV)_i dμ_{c,Q} with the same principal root σ, its matrix P in the fixed basis and the computed slices H_i; generic form for finite measures a.e. supported in a ball and self-adjoint T. No stochastic covariance equation, energy or moment bound.

lem:uniform-halfspace-mass.description: CEK arXiv:1304.0630v1 Lemma 16 proof (54), probability specialization: for a Borel probability measure on a finite-dimensional real inner product space and x₀ in the interior of the convex hull of its support, ∃ m ∈ (0,1] with μ{⟨u, x − x₀⟩ > 0} ≥ m for every unit u (strict open halfspaces; dimension 0 vacuous). Support for Lemma 16 (lem:cek-point-control); not moment-potential existence, not Letwin's constant-8 bound.

lem:cek-point-control.description: CEK arXiv:1304.0630v1 Lemma 16: for a finite Borel measure on a finite-dimensional real inner product space (dimension 0 included) and x₀ interior to the convex hull of its support, one C > 0 chosen before φ gives φ(x₀) ≤ C ∫ φ dμ for every [0,∞]-valued φ with convex real epigraph, a.e.-measurable values and finite integral. Different route for (54) (finite product of ball masses, then normalization).

lem:legendre-convexification.description: Extended-real Legendre transform on a real inner product space: order reversal, Fenchel, φ** ≤ φ, φ*** = φ* for proper φ, lower semicontinuity and convex epigraph for every input; CEK (61) lower truncation and its biconjugate convexification preserving the transform; monotone conjugate mass. Proposition 12 truncation support; the maximiser is thm:cek-variational-maximum.

lem:cek-compactness.description: CEK Lemma 17 in geometric form: finite Borel μ with 0 ∈ int conv(Supp μ) explicit, [0,∞]-valued convex φ_ℓ with φ_ℓ(0) = 0 and bounded integrals; one subsequence and one nonnegative convex μ-integrable limit satisfy (56a) and (56b) for every additive Haar measure, with finite conjugate mass derived. The Theorem 2 conditions give the interior hypothesis by lem:cek-zero-interior; no composed source-form declaration. Not Theorem 2.

lem:cek-zero-interior.description: CEK proof of Lemma 17 under Theorem 2's conditions: a nonzero finite Borel measure on a finite-dimensional real inner product space with finite first moment, barycenter 0 and no proper linear subspace of full measure has 0 in the interior of the convex hull of its support. Mass not normalized.

lem:cek-coercivity.description: Proposition 12 support for centered full-span probability measures: polynomial conjugate-mass coercivity with the constant chosen before the potential (not Lemma 15's constant), epsilon reduction of every admissible competitor to a truncated biconjugate, affine invariance of the functional, supporting-plane normalization, finite norm baseline.

thm:cek-variational-maximum.description: CEK Proposition 12 (38), reviewed stronger: for a probability measure with finite first moment, barycenter 0 and full span on a finite-dimensional real inner product space and any additive Haar dx, a convex lower semicontinuous μ-integrable φ with ∫ e^{−φ*} dx = 1 maximizes I_μ over every μ-integrable f. Not essential continuity, the moment-measure identification or Theorem 2.

lem:letwin-a4-supports.description: Letwin Lemma A.4 (p. 17) proof steps for a given potential: convex φ with integrable e^{−φ} has a minimum and compact sublevels; self-generator Lφ = dim E − ⟨∇V(∇φ), ∇φ⟩ and its uniform bound for bounded gradient image; composition rule, coefficient extraction, pointwise defect domination and continuity of L f; energy identity and weighted energy bound. No minimum, cutoff or energy premise.

lem:letwin-a4-cutoffs.description: Letwin Lemma A.4 (p. 17) for every potential in the source class (smooth convex φ, bounded gradient image K, V smooth near closure K, Monge–Ampère, PD Hessian, ∫e^{−φ} = 1; any finite dimension, any Haar measure): cutoffs χ_R = η((φ − min φ + 1)/R) for all real R ≥ 1, smooth, compactly supported, [0,1]-valued, monotone to 1, with ∫|Lχ_R| dν ≤ C/R, and the natural-index form with C/(n+1). The source-class properties are hypotheses; the moment map is not constructed.

lem:letwin-a5-cutoffs.description: Letwin Lemma A.5 (p. 18) with the cutoffs as a premise: for a given potential as in (2.2), bounded smooth f with Lf + cf ≥ 0 (c > 0) and cutoffs with the conclusions of Lemma A.4, Lf ∈ L¹(ν) and ∫Lf dν = 0; generic Fatou/dominated-convergence core. Composed with A.4 only in the uniform-interval client, not as a general statement.

lem:letwin-uniform-interval-source.description: For K = (−√3, √3) and V ≡ log(2√3): the explicit potential φ(y) = 2 log cosh(√3y/2) + log(4/√3) is in the source class of Letwin Lemmas A.4–A.5 (gradient range inclusion, Monge–Ampère, PD Hessian, ∫e^{−φ} = 1), and f = tanh²(√3y/2) is smooth, bounded, nonconstant with Lf = 1 − 3tanh² and Lf + 2f ≥ 0. Range inclusion only; no pushforward claim.

lem:letwin-uniform-interval-client.description: Letwin Lemma A.5 for the uniform-interval potential (not a uniform-target pushforward or moment-map producer): Lf ∈ L¹(ν) and ∫Lf dν = 0 for f = tanh²(√3y/2), by the source package, the natural-index A.4 cutoffs and A.5 (C = 1, c = 2); no integral-zero premise. A concrete client, not Letwin Theorem 2.5 or 1.2.

lem:weak-finite-linear-combination.description: Generic, one fixed direction: a finite real combination of weak derivatives (any finite set, possibly empty; signed coefficients) is the weak derivative of the combination, with compact-local L2 density; no global L2, boundedness or C1/C2 regularity of the f_i.

lem:weak-finite-product.description: Generic, one fixed direction: L-infinity factors with compact-local L2 weak derivatives give the Leibniz weak derivative of a finite product (empty product included), L2 on compact sets; no global L2, C1/C2 regularity of the rough factors or finite volume.

lem:weak-determinant.description: Generic, one fixed direction: bounded weak matrix fields over any finite index type (empty, singleton) and independent ambient dimension: det A has the signed permutation-polynomial weak derivative, L2 on compact sets; no symmetry, positivity or invertibility. For every real matrix S and every direction v along which the entries of H (bounded by M) have weak derivatives DH that are L2 on compact sets, every entry of S H S is bounded explicitly and has weak derivative the corresponding entry of S DH S, again L2 on compact sets. Then for every globally bounded locally integrable eta with coordinate weak derivatives a_i in L2 on every compact set, both pairings below are integrable and int eta (tr((Hess u)^-1 Hess chi) - DV(grad u)(grad chi)) e^{-u} = -int sum_ij (Hess u)^-1_ij a_i d_j chi e^{-u}.

lem:letwin-weak-trace-contraction.description: This is the weak counterpart of the trace contraction (2.8)/(2.10) in the proof of Letwin Theorem 2.5. Let H, R and E be matrix fields, T a tensor field and rho a continuous weight. Assume H has globally essentially bounded entries, the entries of T and of the fluxes J_ija = sum_b R_ba T_bij are L2 on every compact set, E is locally integrable, and rho sum_a J_ija (psi T_alk + d_a psi H_lk) tested against every compactly supported C1 psi equals minus the integral of rho E_ij psi H_lk. Then for every real matrix B, the density g = 2 tr(B H B E) + 2 sum_ij R_ij tr(B T_i B T_j) is locally integrable and, for every compactly supported C1 psi, the contracted flux sum_j (sum_i R_ij 2 tr(B H B T_i)) d_j psi weighted by rho integrates to minus the integral of rho g psi, with all terms integrable. All finite dimensions; no Hessian, potential or source premise.

lem:letwin-trace-density-positivity.description: For positive semidefinite matrices B, H, R, W and symmetric matrices T_i, with G_R the trace Gram matrix (G_R)_ij = tr(R T_i R T_j), the quantity 2 tr(B H B (-H + H W H + G_R)) + 2 sum_ij R_ij tr(B T_i B T_j) + 2 tr(B H B H) is nonnegative.

lem:letwin-trace-gram-comparison.description: For a positive definite H, a symmetric B and a fully symmetric three-tensor T, sum_ij (H^-1)_ij tr(B T_i B T_j) <= tr(B H B G), where G_ij = tr(H^-1 T_i H^-1 T_j); this is Letwin (2.12) in trace-Gram coordinates. For positive semidefinite B and W and positive definite H, the quantity D = sum_ij (H^-1)_ij tr(B T_i B T_j) satisfies 0 <= D and 4 D <= g + 2 tr(B H B H), where g = 2 tr(B H B (-H + H W H + G)) + 2 D is the weak trace density.

lem:letwin-regular-moment-bounded-weak-c.description: For the actual source law, under the exact original R0 hypotheses (n > 0, isotropic 1_K exp(-W) dx with K compact and convex with nonempty interior, W smooth and kappa-uniformly convex), the same u, L, LF, T and the same common cutoff family as the weak cutoffs (whole earlier payload retained) satisfy, for every r >= 1 and every globally bounded locally integrable eta with coordinate weak derivatives in L2 on every compact set, the rough inverse-Hessian cutoff-generator identity. No source premise is added.

lem:weak-ordinary-diffusion-pairing.description: Let U be C1 with int e^{-U} = 1, v be smooth and compactly supported, and eta be globally bounded and locally integrable with coordinate weak derivatives a_i in L2 on every compact set. Then eta Lv and sum_i a_i d_i v are integrable for the tilted measure e^{-U} dx and int eta Lv dnu = -int sum_i a_i d_i v dnu, where L is the ordinary weighted Laplacian; no inverse-Hessian object is used.

lem:ordinary-diffusion-coercivity-lipsch.description: On a finite-dimensional real inner product space, let U be C1 and globally Lipschitz with Lipschitz gradient and integrable e^{-U}. For every smooth compactly supported f, <D(grad U) grad f, grad f> and (Lf)^2 are integrable for the tilted measure and the integral of the first is at most the integral of the second. This is the Lipschitz-gradient sibling of compact_ordinary_diffusion_coercivity.

lem:letwin-weak-brascamp-lieb.description: This is Letwin Lemma A.6 at C^{1,1} regularity for a given potential. Let nu = e^{-U} dx be a log-concave probability measure with U C1, globally Lipschitz, with Lipschitz gradient, int e^{-U} = 1 and almost everywhere positive definite coordinate Hessian. For every globally bounded locally integrable eta with coordinate weak derivatives a in L2 on every compact set and nu-integrable inverse-Hessian energy <a, (Hess U)^-1 a>, Var_nu eta <= int <a, (Hess U)^-1 a> dnu. The Hilbert-closure helpers it shares with the scalar Brascamp-Lieb owner are public there.

lem:matrix-product-entry-trace.description: For symmetric S and D and arbitrary A, sum_ij (S A S)_ij (S D S)_ij = tr((S S) A (S S) D). For symmetric S, arbitrary R and symmetric T_k, the entrywise quadratic forms of the vectors ((S T_k S)_ij)_k against R sum to sum_kl R_kl tr((S S) T_k (S S) T_l). All finite dimensions.

lem:matrix-variance-trace.description: Under a probability measure, for an almost everywhere symmetric random matrix H with L2 entries and symmetric mean M, sum_ij Var(H_ij) = int tr(H H) - tr(M M). All finite dimensions.

thm:letwin-weak-hessian-trace-bound.description: This is the weak C^{1,1} form of Letwin Theorem 2.5 for a given potential, with positive semidefinite B. Let nu = e^{-U} dx with U convex, C1, globally Lipschitz, with Lipschitz gradient, int e^{-U} = 1 and almost everywhere positive definite Hessian; let T be a weak Hessian tensor in L2 on every compact set, and let the inverse Hessian entries be essentially bounded on every compact set. Assume as hypotheses that the Hessian entries are nu-integrable with mean Id, that D = sum_kl (Hess U)^-1_kl tr(B T_k B T_l) is nu-integrable and that the half-energy bound int D dnu <= (1/2) int tr(B Hess U B Hess U) dnu holds. Then tr(B Hess U B Hess U) is nu-integrable and its integral is at most 2 tr(B B). The mean and half-energy inputs remain visible hypotheses; only the actual source producer discharges them.

lem:symmetric-trace-integral-ae.description: For an arbitrary measure and finite index type, let H have measurable entries and be positive semidefinite almost everywhere. If tr(A H A H) is integrable with integral at most 2 tr(A A) for every positive semidefinite A, then the same holds for every symmetric B, singular or indefinite. This is the almost-everywhere version of symmetric_trace_integral_extension.

lem:integrable-weak-divergence.description: If g is the weak directional derivative of f along v against compactly supported C1 tests and f and g are globally integrable, then int g = 0. Every dimension, including zero, and every direction. The proof body is the accepted S1 API output, copied verbatim.

lem:tilted-ibp-bounded-lipschitz.description: Let U be globally Lipschitz with int e^{-U} = 1 and eta be bounded and globally Lipschitz. For every direction v, D_v eta and eta D_v U are integrable for the tilted measure e^{-U} dx and int D_v eta dnu = int eta D_v U dnu. All dimensions.

lem:c1-gradient-chain.description: For C1 functions u and f and a point y where grad u is differentiable, d_i (f o grad u)(y) = sum_j (Hess u)_ij(y) (grad f)_j(grad u(y)). This is the C1 counterpart of chain_coordinate; all dimensions.

lem:weak-source-stein-identity.description: Let u be C1 and globally Lipschitz with Lipschitz gradient and int e^{-u} = 1, and let nu = e^{-u} dx. For every C1, bounded and globally Lipschitz test f and every coordinate i, d_i u f(grad u) and sum_j (Hess u)_ij d_j f(grad u) are nu-integrable and int d_i u f(grad u) dnu = int sum_j (Hess u)_ij d_j f(grad u) dnu. This is the latent source coupling identity behind Lemma 2.7 at C^{1,1} regularity; no Stein kernel is constructed and no target inverse is used.

lem:compact-source-dual-bound.description: Let P be a measure on a latent space, Z a measurable map with P.map Z = mu for a probability law mu, and F a latent field in L2(P). If a smooth compactly supported h satisfies the latent source identity int <x, v> h dmu = int <F, grad h(Z)> dP, then (int <x, v> h dmu)^2 <= (int |F|^2 dP) (int |Dh|^2 dmu). Arbitrary latent space and all dimensions. The source identity and the L2 field remain inputs; this is the compact dual Cauchy-Schwarz step that supplies the dual bound directly, without a target Stein kernel.

lem:gaussian-directional-identity.description: Under gaussianLaw s with s > 0, in every dimension, for every C1, bounded and globally Lipschitz f and every direction v, <x, v> f and D_v f are integrable and int <x, v> f = (2 s)^-1 int D_v f. This supports the Gaussian smoothing step; no product coupling is asserted.

thm:letwin-regular-moment-weak-stein-cou.description: For the actual source law, under the exact original R0 hypotheses (n > 0, isotropic 1_K exp(-W) dx with K compact and convex with nonempty interior, W smooth and kappa-uniformly convex), there is ONE weak normalized convex globally Lipschitz moment potential u, with constants L, LF and weak Hessian tensor T, that retains the whole earlier payload: R0 regularity (C1, 16/kappa-Lipschitz gradient, 4/kappa centered-difference bound, almost everywhere positive definite Hessian with log-det equation and 16/kappa cap), the weak tensor, first Monge-Ampere and inverse fields, mean Hessian Id under nu = e^{-u} dx, the weak evolution identities, bounded testing, the weak cutoffs and rough cutoff testing, the weak trace contraction, A.5 conservativity int g dnu = 0 and the half energy int D dnu <= (1/2) int tr(B H B H) dnu for every positive semidefinite B. It adds: for EVERY real symmetric B, tr(B H B H) is nu-integrable and int tr(B H B H) dnu <= 2 tr(B B) (Theorem 2.5 with the exact constant 2, weak C^{1,1} form for this witness); the weighted integration by parts int D_v eta dnu = int eta D_v u dnu for every bounded globally Lipschitz eta; and the coordinate source Stein identity for every C1, bounded and globally Lipschitz test. This is not the smooth moment map of Lemma 2.2, not a constructed Stein kernel, and not Theorem 1.2 or the constant-8 bound.

lem:matrix-noise-trace-identities.description: Finite real-matrix trace identities over any finite index type: tr((A + tI)^T (A + tI)) = tr(A^T A) + 2t tr A + n t^2; invariance of tr((AQ)^T AQ) under a symmetric involution Q; tr(SHS) = tr(S^2 H); and tr((SHS)^T SHS) = tr(S^2 H S^2 H) for symmetric S, H.

lem:symmetric-matrix-spectral-geometry.description: For symmetric invertible M with B = sqrt(M^2), S = sqrt B and Q = sign M: B and S are positive semidefinite, Q is symmetric, B^2 = M^2, S^2 = B, SQS = M, Q^2 = I, S is invertible, Q acts self-adjointly and S defines a self-adjoint continuous linear equivalence.

lem:symmetric-invertible-approximation.description: Every symmetric real matrix A over a finite index type is the limit of the symmetric invertible matrices A - r_k I, with 0 < r_k < 1/(k+1) outside the finite real spectrum of A.

lem:matrix-trace-mean-identity.description: For a matrix field H with integrable entries and mean Id under a measure, tr(B H) is integrable with integral tr B for every matrix B.

lem:symmetric-hilbert-schmidt-trace.description: For a symmetric continuous linear operator A and any finite orthonormal basis b, the sum over i, j of <A b_i, b_j>^2 equals tr(A o A).

lem:gradient-affine-precomposition.description: For complete real inner product spaces, a continuous linear S, z and f differentiable at Sx + z, the gradient of y -> f(Sy + z) at x is S* grad f(Sx + z).

lem:matrix-action-algebra.description: The Euclidean action of real n x n matrices equals the Euclidean linear map of the matrix and is multiplicative, additive, homogeneous and unital; (A e_i)_j = A_ji and the sum of |A e_i|^2 is tr(A^T A).

lem:hessian-action-l2.description: If grad u is Lipschitz on R^n, then y -> Hess u(y) v is in L2 of every finite measure, for every v.

lem:quadratic-action-identities.description: Coordinate form sum A_ij x_i x_j = <Ax, x>; the sandwich <Q(Sx), Sx> = <(SQS)x, x> and invariance of the variance of the quadratic form under the pushforward by symmetric S; and e(H(e* v)) + t v = (SHS + tI) v for a self-adjoint equivalence e with the operator of S.

lem:spectral-sign-noise-identity.description: For symmetric invertible M with B = sqrt(M^2), S = sqrt B, Q = sign M, every symmetric H and real t: the sum over i of |(SHS + tI) Q e_i|^2 equals tr(BHBH) + 2t tr(BH) + n t^2.

lem:spectral-noise-energy-integral.description: For probability measures on arbitrary measurable spaces and a measurable, a.e. symmetric matrix field with integrable entries, mean Id and the input trace bound int tr(B'HB'H) <= 2 tr(B'^2) for every symmetric B', the integrated energy of the shifted action is at most 2 tr(M^2) + 2t tr B + n t^2 for symmetric invertible M. No log-concavity or Hessian hypothesis.

lem:quadratic-form-fourth-moment.description: If f is in L4 with values in a real inner product space and A is continuous linear, then <A f, f> is in L2.

lem:finite-combination-variance-continui.description: For a probability measure and finitely many real L2 functions f_i, if the coefficients c_{k,i} converge to b_i then the variance of sum_i c_{k,i} f_i converges to that of sum_i b_i f_i.

lem:quadratic-matrix-variance-continuity.description: For a probability law on R^n with finite fourth moment and matrices A_k -> A, the variance of sum (A_k)_ij x_i x_j converges to that of sum A_ij x_i x_j.

lem:letwin-singular-extension.description: For every probability law on R^n (every n) with finite fourth moment and every real C: if Var(sum B_ij x_i x_j) <= C tr(B^2) for all symmetric invertible B, then for all symmetric B. Stronger than Letwin Lemma A.2 (no isotropy or log-concavity, arbitrary C); proved through B - r_k I outside the spectrum, not M + eps P_0. It does not establish the bound.

lem:centered-noise-quadratic-variance.description: For probability laws mu, nu on a complete separable real inner product space with finite fourth moments, nu centered, and continuous linear A, Var_mu <Ax, x> <= Var_{mu * nu} <Ax, x>.

lem:gaussian-fourth-moments.description: gaussianLaw s (s > 0) has a fourth moment, and fourth moments pass to Gaussian smoothings and to continuous linear images of a probability measure.

lem:gaussian-translated-directional-iden.description: For s > 0, bounded globally Lipschitz C1 h and a, v: int <z, v> h(a + z) = (2s)^-1 int D_v h(a + z) under gaussianLaw s, both integrable.

lem:gaussian-product-latent-map.description: If g pushes the probability measure rho to mu, S is continuous linear and s > 0, then rho x gaussianLaw s pushed by (y, z) -> S(g y) + z is the Gaussian smoothing of S_# mu.

lem:gaussian-smoothed-linear-image-poten.description: For a log-concave probability law with full affine support, a continuous linear equivalence S and s > 0, the Gaussian smoothing of S_# mu is e^{-W} dx with W smooth and convex, and the smoothed probability law is log-concave.

lem:source-directional-affine-stein.description: For C1 globally Lipschitz u with Lipschitz gradient and int e^{-u} = 1: the source Stein identity in a direction v for bounded Lipschitz C1 tests f, and its affine form for tests h(S grad u + z) with continuous linear S.

lem:gaussian-product-source-stein.description: For s > 0, on P = (e^{-u} dx) x gaussianLaw s with Z = S grad u + z: the latent fields are in L2(P), the source and noise pairings are integrable, and int <Z, v> h(Z) dP = int (<S* v, Hess u S* grad h(Z)> + (2s)^-1 D_v h(Z)) dP for bounded Lipschitz C1 h.

lem:gaussian-product-compact-dual.description: With grad u pushing e^{-u} dx to mu, s > 0 and nu_s the Gaussian smoothing of S_# mu: (int <x, v> h d nu_s)^2 <= int |S Hess u S* v + (2s)^-1 v|^2 dP * int |Dh|^2 d nu_s for smooth compactly supported h.

lem:gaussian-noise-limit.description: If a <= b + c (2s)^-1 + d ((2s)^-1)^2 for every s > 0, then a <= b.

lem:gaussian-smoothing-quadratic-varianc.description: For a probability law with finite fourth moment, continuous linear A and s > 0, Var <Ax, x> is at most its variance under the Gaussian smoothing.

lem:gaussian-smoothed-quadratic-h-minus-.description: For log-concave mu with full affine support equal to grad u_# (e^{-u} dx) with u as above, a continuous linear equivalence S, self-adjoint Q and s > 0: the variance of <Qx, x> under the Gaussian smoothing of S_# mu is at most 4 times sum_i int |S Hess u S* Q e_i + (2s)^-1 Q e_i|^2 dP, via the H^-1 inequality on the smooth convex smoothed law.

lem:restricted-exp-logconcave.description: If a probability law mu has density 1_K e^{-W}, with K closed convex and W continuous convex, then 1_K e^{-W} is a Borell density of mu, so mu is log-concave; in particular every regular-class probability law is log-concave.

lem:letwin-operator-matrix-identificatio.description: For every measure mu on R^n: if Var(sum M_ij x_i x_j) <= 8 tr(M^2) for every symmetric M, then mu satisfies LetwinQuadraticBound.

thm:letwin-compact-quadratic-bound.description: letwinCompactBound : LetwinCompactBound: for every n > 0, every compactly supported isotropic log-concave law and every self-adjoint form (singular and indefinite included), variance at most 8 times the squared Hilbert-Schmidt norm in the standard orthonormal basis. Exact compact counterpart of Letwin Theorem 1.2, certified in source form; the noncompact theorem is not covered.

lem:bkl-cutoff-energy.description: BKL (95) in finite-horizon cutoff form, certified (Solutions.LemBklCutoffEnergy): for every d >= 1 (m = d + 1), every compactly supported isotropic log-concave law, unit u, epsilon > 0, T >= 0, all large cutoff radii R and every actual cutoff Eldan process, E_{d+1}(0) + (1/2) int int_0^T gamma_R^2 E_{d+2} <= (d!)^2 153^d + epsilon, from the actual compact constant-8 theorem. A supporting different-route result: the uncut Eldan process, its non-explosion and the literal (68)-(73) are not constructed, and BKL Theorem 4.1 and KLS are not claimed.

The uncut Eldan process and the literal (68)-(73) are not constructed; Theorem 1.1 and KLS are not claimed.
